chunks: Neither does he speak of his own will.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says the Prophet does not speak from his own will?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited alongside its following line to affirm the infallibility (Ismah) of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), distinguishing his inspired speech from mere personal inclination. It serves as a foundational proof for the divine origin of the Quran, countering the Quraysh's claim that he was merely a poet or soothsayer speaking from his own ego.
